requirements.text: The MultiMahjongServer will be designed to reside on a central computer (server) that is connected to a TCP/IP network and has a unique IP address.
The MultiMahjongServer will allow connections from MultiMahjongClients and communicate with them using IP.
The MultiMahjongServer will serve as a node for MultiMahjongClients.

When the user begins the MultiMahjongClient program, they will be able to choose to create a new multi player game, to create a new single player game, to join an existing multi player game, or to quit the program.
The MultiMahjongClient must send this game initialisation information to the MultiMahjongServer so that the MultiMahjongServer can create a new game.
The MultiMahjongClient must only allow players to make moves according to the Chinese rules of Mahjong as described in the rulebook, " How to Play Mah Jong ".
The MultiMahjongClient will inform the user whose turn it is to pick up a tile.
The MultiMahjongClient must inform the user if another player is fishing.
The MultiMahjongClient must inform the user if another player goes Mahjong.
The MultiMahjongClient must inform the user if the hand has ended in a draw.
The game will end when all 4 rounds have been played or if the user chooses to end the game.
The CO must play moves according to the Chinese rules of Mahjong.
The MultiMahjong system is to be written using JDK 1.2 (the Java development kit from Sun Microsystems ).
The CO must respond within 1 minute in both single and multi player modes.
The MultiMahjongServer will have no graphical user interface and will be run using a command prompt.
The MultiMahjongClient will have a graphical user interface that the user will be able to interact with using a mouse and a keyboard.
The GUI is to be designed so that the user can perform all of the Level 1 requirements set out in Section 4 .
The GUI is to be contained within a screen resolution of 800 x 600 pixels.
All graphics will be in 16 bit colour.

Implement input validation on all data received by the MultiMahjongServer from clients to prevent buffer overflows or malicious command execution, and define a secure communication protocol to prevent unauthorized clients from joining games.
The MultiMahjongServer must maintain game state consistency for up to 10 simultaneous games, with a maximum allowable recovery time of 30 seconds for transient network disconnections.
Upon a fatal error, the application must release all network sockets, close file handles, and write a crash dump to the local disk before terminating.
Define a maximum latency for CO moves (e.g., < 500ms) and a maximum latency for move validation/calculation (e.g., < 100ms) to ensure responsive gameplay.
Specify that chat messages must be delivered to all connected clients within 200ms of being sent by the source client.

OPEN: The server architecture allows relaying data between clients, but there is no mention of authentication or authorization mechanisms to prevent unauthorized users from joining games or spoofing other players. - The MultiMahjongServer shall implement a session-based authentication mechanism to ensure that only authorized clients can join a game and that player identities are verified during the session.

OPEN: The requirement for CO response time does not specify behavior if the CO fails to calculate a move within the 1-minute threshold. - If the CO fails to respond within 60 seconds, the system must log a fatal error, terminate the current game session, and notify all connected clients to prevent a deadlock.

OPEN: There is no requirement for data persistence or state recovery in the event of a server crash. - The MultiMahjongServer must implement a periodic state checkpointing mechanism every 5 minutes to allow game resumption after a server-side failure.

OPEN: The server capacity is limited to 10 simultaneous games without specifying the expected network bandwidth or server hardware requirements to support this load. - Specify the minimum server hardware (CPU/RAM) and network throughput required to maintain the 10-game capacity without exceeding the defined latency thresholds.
